interpretive.cite: Roberts v. Ball, Hunt, Hart, Brown & Baerwitz, 57 Cal.App.3d 104 (1976)
interpretive.rule: §1710(2) negligent misrepresentation: positive assertion without reasonable grounds is actionable even without scienter. Fills gap between intentional fraud and non-actionable opinion.

§1710(4) promissory fraud: promise + no intent to perform at time of making + inducing reliance + damage. Pattern evidence of similar broken promises = circumstantial proof of non-intent. Applies to yo-yo financing.

deceit_modes.1710_1: Dealer provided a false CARFAX showing no accidents. If dealer knew vehicle had prior damage: knowing false statement.
deceit_modes.1710_2: If dealer did not 'know' CARFAX was wrong but provided it without reasonable grounds for asserting clean history: negligent misrepresentation.
deceit_modes.1710_3: Dealer had exclusive knowledge of vehicle's true condition (from PDI or prior dealings) and did not disclose: nondisclosure under Lovejoy category 2.
deceit_modes.1710_4: Yo-yo financing: dealer offered firm financing terms to close the deal with no intention or ability to honor them: promissory fraud under Lazar.

redjag_fraud_theory.damages: Purchase price paid minus actual fair market value of the vehicle as delivered (wrong CARFAX, stripped, damaged). Also: Rees-Levering forfeiture + Song-Beverly refund + CLRA actual + §3294 punitive.

proof_strategy: Obtain the CARFAX the dealer provided at sale (compare to true vehicle history)
Obtain pre-delivery inspection (PDI) records from dealer
Obtain financing approval/denial records showing timeline between contract signing and yo-yo demand
Identify similar complaints from other customers against same dealer (pattern evidence for Lazar non-intent theory + §3294 malice/oppression)
Document the actual market value of the vehicle as received (with prior damage disclosed)
